knowledge:
- key_parameters: min_samps_feature_expr=Minimal number of samples where a transcript must be expressed to be kept ;; min_feature_expr=Minimal absolute count threshold for a transcript to be kept ;; min_samps_gene_expr=Minimal number of samples where a gene must be expressed to be kept ;; min_gene_expr=Minimal absolute count threshold for a gene to be kept ;; design=Design matrix defining the full experimental model of interest ;; bb_model=Logical indicating whether to run transcript-level analysis based on the beta-binomial model (only available in DTU) ;; one_way=Logical indicating whether to use a fast shortcut group-fitting algorithm when the design corresponds to multiple group comparisons ;; coef=Character or numeric indicating which column of the design matrix to remove to construct the null model ;; contrast=Numeric vector defining a specific contrast for testing ;; minor_allele_freq=Minimal number of individuals carrying the minor allele for a SNP to be retained in tuQTL analysis ;; speed=Logical indicating whether to calculate a single precision per gene under the null model to speed up tuQTL analysis ;; permutation_mode=Character ("all_genes" or "per_gene") defining the permutation scheme used to assess the null distribution of associations in tuQTL analysis
- alternatives: stageR=Recommended for stage-wise testing (screening and confirmation stages) to properly control FDR and FWER when interpreting both gene-level and transcript-level p-values ;; edgeR=Mentioned as the source of the adapted 'one way' fitting algorithm, grid-based precision estimation, and contrast-based null design calculation
- when_to_use: Use when you have transcript-level count data (e.g., from kallisto or FluxCapacitor) and want to detect differential transcript usage across conditions (DTU) or identify genetic variants associated with changes in transcript ratios (tuQTL)
- pitfalls: Directly interpreting both gene-level and transcript-level adjusted p-values without a stage-wise procedure (like stageR) does not provide appropriate FDR control and should be avoided ;; Precision estimation is highly computationally intensive, so users should increase the number of workers in BPPARAM for larger datasets ;; In tuQTL analysis, running permutation_mode="per_gene" can be extremely slow; "all_genes" is recommended as a faster default ;; Transcript-level analysis (bb_model=TRUE) is currently only implemented for DTU, not tuQTL

workflows.name: differential_transcript_usage
workflows.intent: Perform differential transcript usage (DTU) analysis between experimental conditions, with or without batch effects, using Dirichlet-multinomial and beta-binomial models.
input: pasilla_counts.txt (matrix of transcript counts with feature_id and gene_id columns)
metadata.txt (sample metadata containing sample names, conditions, and optional batch covariates)
workflows.stages: 1. Load counts and sample metadata into a dmDSdata object using dmDSdata() ;; 2. Filter out lowly expressed genes and transcripts using dmFilter() ;; 3. Define the full model design matrix using model.matrix() ;; 4. Estimate precision parameters using dmPrecision() ;; 5. Fit the full model proportions and coefficients using dmFit() ;; 6. Test for differential usage against a null model using dmTest() ;; 7. Extract results using results() and visualize proportions using plotProportions()
workflows.code:
pasilla_samples <- data.frame(sample_id = pasilla_metadata$SampleName, 
  group = pasilla_metadata$condition)
levels(pasilla_samples$group)

d <- dmDSdata(counts = pasilla_counts, samples = pasilla_samples)
d
head(counts(d), 3)
head(samples(d), 3)

plotData(d)

gene_id_subset <- readLines(file.path(data_dir, "gene_id_subset.txt"))
d <- d[names(d) %in% gene_id_subset, ]
d

table(samples(d)$group)

d <- dmFilter(d, min_samps_gene_expr = 7, min_samps_feature_expr = 3,
  min_gene_expr = 10, min_feature_expr = 10)

design_full <- model.matrix(~ group, data = samples(d))
design_full

set.seed(123)
d <- dmPrecision(d, design = design_full)
d
head(mean_expression(d), 3)
common_precision(d)
head(genewise_precision(d))

plotPrecision(d)

library(ggplot2)
ggp <- plotPrecision(d)
ggp + geom_point(size = 4)

d <- dmFit(d, design = design_full, verbose = 1)
d

head(proportions(d))
head(coefficients(d))
head(coefficients(d), level = "feature")

d <- dmTest(d, coef = "groupKD", verbose = 1)
design(d)
head(results(d), 3)

design_null <- model.matrix(~ 1, data = samples(d))
design_null
d <- dmTest(d, design = design_null)
head(results(d), 3)

contrast <- c(0, 1)
d <- dmTest(d, contrast = contrast)
design(d)
head(results(d), 3)

head(results(d, level = "feature"), 3)

plotPValues(d)
plotPValues(d, level = "feature")

res <- results(d)
res <- res[order(res$pvalue, decreasing = FALSE), ]
top_gene_id <- res$gene_id[1]

plotProportions(d, gene_id = top_gene_id, group_variable = "group")
plotProportions(d, gene_id = top_gene_id, group_variable = "group", 
  plot_type = "lineplot")
plotProportions(d, gene_id = top_gene_id, group_variable = "group", 
  plot_type = "ribbonplot")

workflows.name: transcript_usage_qtl
workflows.intent: Identify genetic variants (SNPs) associated with changes in transcript usage (tuQTLs) using a Dirichlet-multinomial model.
input: geuv_counts (matrix of transcript counts with feature_id and gene_id columns)
geuv_genotypes (matrix of SNP genotypes with snp_id column)
workflows.stages: 1. Format counts, genotypes, and sample data frames ;; 2. Create a dmSQTLdata object using dmSQTLdata() with a specified genomic window ;; 3. Filter out lowly expressed features and low-frequency alleles using dmFilter() ;; 4. Estimate precision parameters using dmPrecision() ;; 5. Fit the model proportions using dmFit() ;; 6. Test for tuQTL associations using dmTest() ;; 7. Extract results using results() and visualize proportions using plotProportions()
workflows.code:
colnames(geuv_counts)[c(1,2)] <- c("feature_id", "gene_id")
colnames(geuv_genotypes)[4] <- "snp_id"
geuv_samples <- data.frame(sample_id = colnames(geuv_counts)[-c(1,2)])

d <- dmSQTLdata(counts = geuv_counts, gene_ranges = geuv_gene_ranges,
  genotypes = geuv_genotypes, snp_ranges = geuv_snp_ranges, 
  samples = geuv_samples, window = 5e3)
d

plotData(d, plot_type = "features")
plotData(d, plot_type = "snps")
plotData(d, plot_type = "blocks")

d <- dmFilter(d, min_samps_gene_expr = 70, min_samps_feature_expr = 5,
  minor_allele_freq = 5, min_gene_expr = 10, min_feature_expr = 10)

set.seed(123)
d <- dmPrecision(d)

plotPrecision(d)

d <- dmFit(d)

d <- dmTest(d)
plotPValues(d)
head(results(d))

res <- results(d)
res <- res[order(res$pvalue, decreasing = FALSE), ]

top_gene_id <- res$gene_id[1]
top_snp_id <- res$snp_id[1]

plotProportions(d, gene_id = top_gene_id, snp_id = top_snp_id)
plotProportions(d, gene_id = top_gene_id, snp_id = top_snp_id,
  plot_type = "boxplot2")
